guides.title: Life cycle assessment results
guides.purpose: This directory contains LCA results for one foreground scenario, organized by background scenario and LCIA selection.
inputs: The completed MFA result and one or more prepared background scenarios.

expected_contents.name: <background_and_selection_readable_name>/
expected_contents.description: one result for a background scenario and LCIA selection

tables_and_schemas: Each result contains score, contribution, inventory, carbon consistency, and calculation tables.
units_signs_and_identifiers: Child names are readable background/method selections.
Scores and contributions use the unit recorded for each LCIA category.
guides.pandas_example:
import pandas as pd

scores = pd.read_parquet(
    workspace / "results/<foreground_scenario>/lca_results/<selection>/scores.parquet"
)
reuse_and_refresh: `run_lca` reuses a result when its manifest exists.
`run_lca(refresh=True)` recalculates only the selected LCA results.
scientific_limitations: Each result uses one foreground MFA result and one background scenario. The article assesses the 16 EF 3.1 impact categories against allocated carrying capacities. The ten supported PB-LCIA impact categories provide additional characterization only. Monitoring and target-setting ASRs use EF v3.1 and cumulative GWP100.
Global rows are derived from the 12 regional calculations.

guides.title: Time-explicit LCA result
guides.purpose: This directory contains the LCA tables for one foreground scenario, background scenario, and LCIA selection.
inputs: One completed MFA result, one prepared background scenario, the 12 world regions, and the selected LCIA methods.

expected_contents.name: scores.parquet
expected_contents.description: regional and global environmental burdens summed over 2019-2100, with LCIA method and impact category information

expected_contents.name: annual_scores.parquet
expected_contents.description: regional and global environmental burdens for each year from 2019 to 2100

expected_contents.name: annual_life_cycle_stage_scores.parquet

expected_contents.name: life_cycle_stage_scores.parquet

expected_contents.name: contributions.parquet

expected_contents.name: stage_contributions.parquet
expected_contents.description: contribution detail for the same selected upstream analysis years, separated by life cycle stage

expected_contents.name: structural_paths.parquet

expected_contents.name: structural_edges.parquet

expected_contents.name: structural_attribution.parquet

expected_contents.name: inventory_authority.parquet

expected_contents.name: manifest.json
expected_contents.description: MFA and background inputs, methods, Timex settings, file hashes, and completion status

tables_and_schemas: The manifest records each file's columns, data types, row count, content identifier, and hash.

Flow coverage has one row per source_table, source_flow_name and product. It reports the flow classification, known constituent axis, first/last source year, persisted/nonzero row counts, total_amount in Mt, related burden/provider lists, stage, mapping basis, event-year rule, cut-off role and explanation. The lists name related services.

Annual and 2019-2100 stage scores sum to the corresponding total environmental burdens. Period totals cover 2019--2100. Global scores sum the 12 regional scores for the same LCIA method, impact category, and year or period; global shares are calculated from those totals. Regional and global native-activity and elementary-flow detail are ranked independently by contribution_norm, retaining up to 100 native activities or flows plus each view's own exact residual. Global ranking uses complete regional contributions before regional selection. `modelled_direct` identifies contributions from pyToCE's process models for polyamide fibers (PA6 and PA66), including their wastewater and waste treatment. Each row names the process in `receiving_function` and the environmental flow (for example, a CO2 emission) in `elementary_flow_name`. Its `score` is included in the reported total for the same region, year, and impact category. These rows remain outside the native-activity limit. Select one `contribution_view` when reading detail; provider, native-activity and elementary-flow rows are alternative decompositions of the same burdens.

Within each stage, native activity and elementary flow detail are ranked independently by `contribution_norm`, retaining up to 25 entries and each view's own residual. Separately labeled `modelled_direct` rows remain outside the native activity limit.

The parent MFA material_realization.parquet records manufacturing input, finished output and manufacturing losses, recovered resin, chemical recycling products, and recovered or virgin monomer consumption. Manufacturing input covers both the finished output and the losses. Conversion burdens are calculated once from the finished output; activation_lineage.parquet records the corresponding LCA supplier demands.

The mismanaged_waste_fate and mismanaged_waste_fate_closure tables, and carbon_consistency.csv, cover fixed per-kilogram provider services and retain their constituent/product coordinates. Actual PA6/PA66 fiber receiving is reported separately: pa_receiving_physical_events.parquet records processing, waste fates and balances; pa_receiving_inventory.parquet records supplier demands and elementary flows; direct_treatment_carbon_flows.parquet records the attributable CO2, CO and CH4. The fixed-service diagnostics compare their own prepared service demands. Stage and upstream contribution totals include both kinds of inventory.

PA receiving inventory has one row per actual event, source anchor, dump class, process and native endpoint. Its supplier rows enter the existing native matrix; elementary rows enter the same inventory before characterization. Source records describe the actual coefficient authorities. Event JSON preserves typed input fields; receiving JSON preserves calculated phase, load, energy and discharge fields. Emission, native-factor and phosphate-compartment dictionaries use coordinate/value records: coordinates retain the complete source tuple, and values retain its declared unit.
units_signs_and_identifiers: The unit column records the registered LCIA unit for each impact category.

share is unavailable when the total score is zero or its magnitude is at most 1e-10 times contribution_norm, the sum of absolute characterized contributions. This relative cancellation criterion is unchanged by equivalent unit rescaling. Per-unit provider values compare the signed provider demand with the sum of absolute demands in the same way. A zero_total_activity status means both per-unit values are unavailable because every demand is zero; near_zero_total_activity indicates cancellation: `effective_unit_score` is unavailable, while `effective_unit_norm` remains defined when absolute demand is nonzero. Scores, absolute contributions and norm_share remain unchanged.

Flow coverage totals include the full MFA parent period, including history. Aggregate C and Other Elements sum to polymer mass. Select one table, quantity, and process step for each total. Only 2019-2100 events generate reported LCA burdens.
Foreground scenario, background scenario, world region, stage year, provider, activity, elementary flow, LCIA method, and impact category remain separate columns.

Ordinary mapped service activation amounts use the reference quantity declared by `mapping_basis`. Polymerization and each ethylene/propylene supply use kilograms of destination-polymer output represented by that service; their demands retain the stated service units. PA receiving activations retain the native reference unit recorded in `endpoint_unit`, which can be mass, volume or energy.

Detailed treatment carbon uses principal_carbon_fraction for the share of each owner gas flow attributable to the treated principal. For TPS this is the actual principal carbon origin, retained separately even when biogenic and DAC carbon share a native non-fossil flow. flow_amount and carbon_amount already include that fraction; use the recorded amount directly. TPS provider_demand_amount is the full demand repeated for each origin comparison and should be counted once per demand coordinate. Internal signed kg and cubic-meter treatment references are normalized once.

PA receiving quantities use endpoint_unit, including kg, cubic meters and energy units. amount equals unweighted_amount times temporal_share; use the recorded amount directly. Event JSON remains unweighted on its already allocated dump-class basis: apply temporal_share once across anchors. Nested parent and child indicators describe connected process quantities. Principal-origin amounts are portions of the same endpoint quantity, portions of one exchange. The detailed carbon table identifies each modeled PA function and its calculated carbon flows. Its receiving_flow_amount is a repeated gas-flow denominator across origin rows and should be counted once per flow coordinate; flow_amount and carbon_amount already contain origin and time weighting.
Virgin-feedstock route selects the supply technology; ultimate carbon origin attributes carbon in the product.
guides.pandas_example:
import pandas as pd

result = workspace / "results/<foreground_scenario>/lca_results/<selection>"
scores = pd.read_parquet(result / "annual_scores.parquet")
print(scores.query("year == 2050").head())
reuse_and_refresh: `run_lca` reuses the result when its manifest exists.
`run_lca(refresh=True)` recalculates this LCA result only. The existing result is replaced only after the new calculation completes.
scientific_limitations: Annual environmental burdens assign each life cycle stage to its activity year. Releases contained in a process inventory, including long-term landfill emissions, are attributed to that activity year; LCIA characterization factors remain constant across years.
Reporting ends in 2100 with stock still in use retained.

Provider locations follow their source inventories. MFA regions identify where the modeled plastics flows occur. The fixed-service carbon and mismanaged-waste diagnostics cover their listed per-kilogram services. Read them with the MFA balances and the separate actual PA6/PA66 fiber receiving ledgers.

Background and auxiliary fossil emissions remain in the LCA while the comparison tracks principal plastic carbon from the MFA. Landfill wastewater and sludge gases use source-derived waste fractions; both fossil and non-fossil diagnostics exclude flocculant carbon.

PA mass-balance ledgers report the modeled energy and phase quantities. The treatment-carbon diagnostic covers CO2, CO and CH4 attributable to the principal material. Auxiliary burdens remain fully characterized and are excluded from this principal-carbon attribution.
Treatment carbon is a nonadditive diagnostic. The mfa_carbon_boundary column distinguishes chemical preparation gate carbon from hydrothermal processed-feed carbon.
Mechanical recycling reports managed incineration and landfill separately from principal entering wastewater and air.

The open-burning fraction uses the global uncollected-waste split from Cottom et al.; the non-burned remainder is assigned to open dumping. Both fractions apply to every world region and year. Open dumping uses the fixed portfolio of five ecoinvent infiltration classes.

Dry tire-family SBR uses native waste-rubber incineration and a 25/75 PS/PE analogue for landfill, open burning and open dumping. Non-tire SBR in Others uses the finished compound-22 composition, including its auxiliary materials, and the corresponding waste-treatment calculations.
